## Simple explanation

Prompt engineering is the process of shaping what a language model is asked
to do and how the request is presented. It includes clarifying instructions,
providing relevant context, and testing outputs against examples.

## Technical explanation

Prompt engineering develops and evaluates input templates, message
structures, examples, and constraints for a model and task. Techniques
include zero-shot instructions, few-shot examples, decomposition, and
structured-output requests. Performance depends on the model, data, and
evaluation method.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Prompt design can improve task accuracy without changing model weights, but
prompt changes can also create regressions. Treating prompts as versioned
software and evaluating them on representative cases makes behavior changes
measurable.

## How it works

An engineer defines the desired behavior and provides useful instructions
and context. They run a set of test inputs, assess outcomes using task
metrics or human review, and revise the prompt. Production systems should
also monitor failures and protect against untrusted content.

## Practical example

For classifying customer feedback, a prompt can define the available labels,
explain how to handle ambiguous cases, and request a structured result.
Testing should include examples from each label and edge cases that were not
used while writing the prompt.

## Common misconceptions

- Prompt engineering does not reliably compensate for missing knowledge or
  unsuitable model capabilities.
- Few-shot examples can help, but poor, inconsistent, or biased examples
  can make results worse.
